classification.difficultyReason: Identify the ladder as the hypotenuse in the supplied wall diagram, apply Pythagoras and round the positive square root to the requested precision.

content.prompt: The foot of a ladder is placed 1.2 m from a vertical wall. If the ladder reaches 7 m up the wall, what is the length of the ladder? Answer in metres to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Ladder rises to the right against a vertical outlined wall. Ground distance is labelled beneath the ladder foot and wall; a vertical dimension arrow lies to the right of the wall.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal distance 1.2 m, vertical height 7 m, and right angle between the ground and wall. The ladder is the hypotenuse.
spec.answerVisibility: The ladder length is not supplied.

answer.worked:
The ladder is the hypotenuse. Let its length be $h$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=a^2+b^2\\h^2&=1.2^2+7^2\\h^2&=1.44+49\\h^2&=50.44\\h&=\sqrt{50.44}\\h&\approx7.10\end{align*}$$
The ladder is $7.10\text{ m}$ long, to 2 decimal places.
